blocks.arabic_text: امْرِئئٍ مُسْلِمٍ تَحْضُرُهُ صَلَاةٌ مَكْتُوبَةٌ فَيُحْسِنُ وُضُوءَهَا وَخُشُوعَهَا وَرُكُوعَهَا إِلَّا كَانَتْ كَفَّارَةً لِمَا قَبْلَهَا مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ مَالَمْ يُؤْتِ كَبِيرَةً، وَذلِكَ الدَّهْرَ كُلَّهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم باب فضل الوضوء ...صحيح مسلم:١ /٢٠٦. طبع داراحيا ءالتراث العر بي
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Uthman (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said, “Whichever Muslim, when the time of a Fard Salah comes, makes Wudu well, prays with great devotion and makes ruku' well in it, that Salah becomes an expiation for his previous sins, as long as he does not commit major sins. He will keep receiving this virtue forever.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- Khushu' in Salah means that along with the greatness and fear of Allah being in the heart, the limbs of the body should also be at rest. As for devotion, directing the gaze to the place of sajdah when standing, onto the toes in ruku', onto the nose in sajdah, and onto the lap when sitting, is part of khushu'.
(Bayan al-Qur'an, Sharh Sunan Abi Dawud)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ خَالِدِنِ الْجُهَنِيِّ ﵁ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ فَأَحْسَنَ وُضُوءَهُ، ثُمَّ صَلَّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَا يَسْهُو فِيهِمَا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ.
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Zaid ibn Khalid Juhani (RA) has narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said, “Whoever makes Wudu well and prays two rak'ahs without forgetfulness in them (giving complete attention towards Allah), all his previous sins are forgiven.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَامِرِنِ الْجُهَنِيِّ ﵁ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: مَا مِنْ
